docs.title: pystepdowner
docs.text:
A tool to enforce the Stepdown Rule (from Uncle Bob's Clean Code) in your Python files.

The Stepdown Rule states that code should be readable from top to bottom. Every function should be followed by those at the next level of abstraction so that we can read the program, descending one level of abstraction at a time as we read down the list of functions.

pystepdowner analyzes your Python files and rearranges functions and methods to adhere to this rule, prioritizing source-code call order and correctly handling complex dependency graphs.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
You can install pystepdowner as a global CLI tool using uv (recommended):

# Install from PyPI
uv tool install pystepdowner

# Or install from source locally
uv tool install .

Alternatively, you can install it into any Python environment using standard pip:

pip install pystepdowner

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: The CLI provides two main commands: fmt and rw.

docs.title: 1. fmt: Format and Print to Output
docs.text:
Use the fmt command to format a single file and output the result to your terminal. This is useful for previewing changes without modifying the actual file.

pystepdowner fmt -i my_script.py

docs.title: 2. rw: Rewrite Files
docs.text: Use the rw command to format and rewrite files. You can rewrite a single file or an entire directory recursively.

docs.title: Rewrite a Single File and Save to a New Location
Rewrite an Entire Directory In-Place
docs.text:
This will recursively find and format all .py files inside the target directory.

pystepdowner rw -i src/

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
pystepdowner transforms bottom-up code into top-down code, putting high-level logic before the helpers it calls.

Before: 

def load_user(user_id: int) -> dict:
    return {"id": user_id, "name": "Alice"}


def format_user(user: dict) -> str:
    return f"{user['id']}: {user['name']}"


def user_controller(user_id: int) -> dict:
    user = load_user(user_id)
    return {"body": format_user(user)}

After running pystepdowner rw -i my_script.py: 

def user_controller(user_id: int) -> dict:
    user = load_user(user_id)
    return {"body": format_user(user)}


def load_user(user_id: int) -> dict:
    return {"id": user_id, "name": "Alice"}


def format_user(user: dict) -> str:
    return f"{user['id']}: {user['name']}"

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Topological Sorting: Correctly sequences nested function calls and handles mutual recursion.
  • Class Methods: Seamlessly reorders methods within a class definition.
  • Automatic Annotations: Automatically inserts from __future__ import annotations if an annotation dependency is moved below its definition to avoid NameError.
  • Comment Preservation: Retains module-level and function-level comments in their correct logical blocks.

docs.title: Cases
docs.text: Case names follow the pattern: {subject kind} subject -> {reference cardinality} {target kind} reference(s) via {reference form}.

docs.title: Function subject -> one function reference via direct call
docs.text:
Subject: one module-level function. References: one module-level function. Reference form: direct call. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declaration.

Before:

def b() -> str:
    return "b"


def a() -> str:
    return b()

After:

def a() -> str:
    return b()


def b() -> str:
    return "b"

docs.title: Function subject -> two function references via direct calls
docs.text:
Subject: one module-level function. References: two module-level functions. Reference form: direct calls. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declarations in reference order.

Before:

def c() -> str:
    return "c"


def b() -> str:
    return "b"


def a() -> str:
    return b() + c()

After:

def a() -> str:
    return b() + c()


def b() -> str:
    return "b"


def c() -> str:
    return "c"

docs.title: Function subject -> one function reference via dictionary value
docs.text:
Subject: one module-level function. References: one module-level function. Reference form: dictionary value selected by argument key. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declaration.

Before:

def b() -> str:
    return "b"


def a(key: str) -> str:
    handlers = {"b": b}
    handler = handlers[key]
    return handler()

After:

def a(key: str) -> str:
    handlers = {"b": b}
    handler = handlers[key]
    return handler()


def b() -> str:
    return "b"

docs.title: Function subject -> two function references via dictionary values
docs.text:
Subject: one module-level function. References: two module-level functions. Reference form: dictionary values selected by argument key. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declarations in dictionary insertion order.

Before:

def c() -> str:
    return "c"


def b() -> str:
    return "b"


def a(key: str) -> str:
    handlers = {"b": b, "c": c}
    handler = handlers[key]
    return handler()

After:

def a(key: str) -> str:
    handlers = {"b": b, "c": c}
    handler = handlers[key]
    return handler()


def b() -> str:
    return "b"


def c() -> str:
    return "c"

docs.title: Instance method subject -> one instance method reference via direct call
docs.text:
Subject: one instance method. References: one instance method. Reference form: direct call. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declaration.

Before:

class Greeting:
    def format_name(self) -> str:
        return "Ada"

    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}!"

After:

class Greeting:
    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}!"

    def format_name(self) -> str:
        return "Ada"

docs.title: Instance method subject -> two instance method references via direct calls
docs.text:
Subject: one instance method. References: two instance methods. Reference form: direct calls. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declarations in reference order.

Before:

class Greeting:
    def format_punctuation(self) -> str:
        return "!"

    def format_name(self) -> str:
        return "Ada"

    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}{self.format_punctuation()}"

After:

class Greeting:
    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}{self.format_punctuation()}"

    def format_name(self) -> str:
        return "Ada"

    def format_punctuation(self) -> str:
        return "!"

docs.title: Instance method subject -> one static method reference via direct call
docs.text:
Subject: one instance method. References: one static method. Reference form: direct call. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declaration.

Before:

class Greeting:
    @staticmethod
    def format_name() -> str:
        return "Ada"

    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}!"

After:

class Greeting:
    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}!"

    @staticmethod
    def format_name() -> str:
        return "Ada"

docs.title: Instance method subject -> instance method and static method references via direct calls
docs.text:
Subject: one instance method. References: one instance method and one static method. Reference form: direct calls. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declarations in reference order.

Before:

class Greeting:
    @staticmethod
    def format_punctuation() -> str:
        return "!"

    def format_name(self) -> str:
        return "Ada"

    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}{Greeting.format_punctuation()}"

After:

class Greeting:
    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}{Greeting.format_punctuation()}"

    def format_name(self) -> str:
        return "Ada"

    @staticmethod
    def format_punctuation() -> str:
        return "!"
